messages.subject: perpendicular or radial distance truncation ?
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,

I'm working in the French Southern Territories and we are using Distance=20
sampling to estimate density of various birds breeding over there=20
especially burrowing petrels and ducks.
We're using line transects to sample Kerguelen pintail and try to=20
estimate the size of the population. For each group of duck contacted we=20
measure the radial distance and the angle with a laser range finder and=20
count the number of pintail (cluster size) on both side of the transect.
Now I am analysing the data with Distance but I don't know what is the=20
best way to truncate my sample (the 5%) :
1/ in Distance I enter the radial distance and the angle measured in the=20
field and use the radial distance to calculate the truncation (here 141m)=
 or
2/ in Distance I enter the radial distance and the angle measured in the=20
field and use the perpendicular distance to calculate the truncation=20
(here 86,7m) or
3/ in Distance I enter the perpendicular distance (calculated back in=20
the office) and use the perpendicular distance to calculate the=20
truncation (here 86,7).

Which one of the 3 possibilities above should I use to analyse my data?

Thanks in advance for your time.

Fabrice

--=20
Fabrice Le Bouard
Technicien de recherche des inventaires et suivis ornithologiques et
mammalogiques de la r=E9serve naturelle des Terres australes fran=E7aises=
.

messages.subject: Re: perpendicular or radial distance truncation ?
messages.body_plain:
Fabrice:

The truncation distance you want to use is perpendicular distance from
the transect line.  But Distance will permit you to simply enter a
percentage (say 5%) and Distance will transform that percentage into a
perpendicular distance.  Recognise also that Distance will calculate
perpendicular distances from your entry of radial distance and angles.

So my suggestion to you is
a) enter your sightings into Distance using radial distance and angle as
measured  in the field
b) request that Distance truncate 5% of sightings with the greatest
perpendicular distances.  Accomplish this using the radio button
selection shown in this screen capture at this Dropbox link

https://www.dropbox.com/s/brm2t7jj0z4pwqu/fabrice.JPG
